title: BENCH: warm-pool allocation latency idle and loaded
description:
Measure the actual request-path cost of allocating from a pre-filled warm pool. This is the benchmark that proves whether m80 reaches the sub-200 ms clean-VM target in the path callers will actually use.

## Scope

- Add or extend a benchmark under crates/m80-firecracker/benches/ that pre-fills a pool, then measures allocation -> first successful exec -> release/discard.
- Run idle and loaded cells. Loaded should use the existing stress-ng shape so results compare with cold-launch and snapshot-restore data.
- Report P50, P95, max, success count, and pool-refill lag.
- Compare against the current measured baselines: persistent sequential exec ~20.6 ms, direct snapshot restore 274.204 ms P50 idle / 444.972 ms P50 loaded, and cold launch in docs/perf/cold-launch.md.
- Persist machine-readable output next to the existing behavior JSON snapshots, and summarize in docs/perf/cold-launch.md or a dedicated warm-pool perf doc.

## Acceptance

- N >= 50 idle allocations from a pre-filled pool produce P50/P95/max and success count.
- N >= 50 loaded allocations produce the same metrics, or the doc records a diagnostics-first failure with logs/artifacts.
- The benchmark distinguishes request-path allocation latency from background refill latency.
- docs/behaviors/lifecycle or docs/behaviors/snapshot includes a JSON artifact with the exact numbers.
- CHANGELOG records the measured result, including whether sub-200 ms was achieved.

title: m80 quickstart: first-30s constrained-process UX
description:
Split first-touch UX from CI verification. Quickstart targets clean machine -> artifacts/profile -> `m80 run -- echo hello` quickly; smoke targets CI exit codes.

Why:
- The product story is no longer "launch a VM". It is "run a process with a constrained view of the host". Quickstart must teach that from the first command.
- The gap is mostly missing prebuilts, no default image/profile story, and no quickstart path.

Scope:
- scripts/quickstart.sh downloads the latest release tarball, verifies sha256s, places kernel/rootfs/manifest in expected paths, resolves the default image/profile, runs `m80 run -- echo hello`, and prints next-step pointers for `--workspace`, `--egress none`, `--tty`, image/profile selection, and `warm` if available.
- `m80 quickstart` or equivalent in-binary entrypoint may perform the same flow without requiring shell access.
- README top fold points at the quickstart command.

Out of scope:
- CI smoke remains separate.
- No interactive prompts; quickstart is non-interactive end-to-end.
- No agent-specific setup.

Acceptance:
- A clean machine with no m80 checkout can run the documented invocation and see `hello` from `m80 run -- echo hello` in less than 60s wall clock, assuming release artifacts exist.
- README documents quickstart and points at it from the top fold.
- smoke and quickstart have zero overlapping logic.
- Quickstart docs use constrained-process and image/profile vocabulary, not VM lifecycle vocabulary.

Dependency:
- Blocked by m80-6jni.3 or equivalent prebuilt artifact release lane plus the command/profile docs that define the final surface.

title: Marker-file readiness probe to beat SmolVM's polling latency
description:
Replace m80-firecracker's `phase_12b_ready_probe` polling loop with a
stat-based marker probe — IF Firecracker actually creates a host-visible
file when m80-guestd binds its vsock listener. Verification is gating;
see leaf 1.

## Background

Today's `phase_12b_ready_probe`
(crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch.rs:423):
- Calls `Channel::open_uds_only` (UDS connect + write `CONNECT 9001`
  + read `OK` line) every 500ms with a 30s deadline. The 5s
  read timeout caps each attempt.
- Each successful attempt is roughly a UDS handshake's worth of work.
- Under host load the probe occasionally times out before guestd binds.

SmolVM's `wait_for_ssh`:
- `socket.connect()` + 32-byte banner sniff at 100ms intervals,
  then full handshake once the banner appears. 60s budget.

## Marker-file premise — UNVERIFIED

The dossier hypothesis: when m80-guestd does
`VsockListener::bind((VMADDR_CID_ANY, 9001))`, Firecracker creates the
host-side companion file `<vsock_uds>_<port>` (e.g.
`<jail>/vsock.sock_9001`) inside the chroot, and stat'ing that file is
a near-zero-cost readiness signal.

CAUTION — Firecracker's official vsock docs
(https://github.com/firecracker-microvm/firecracker/blob/main/docs/vsock.md)
describe `<uds>_<port>` only in the *opposite* direction: as the file
the **host application** is expected to be listening on so that
**guest-initiated** connections can be forwarded by Firecracker. There
is no documented host filesystem artifact created when the guest binds
a port and waits for host-initiated connects (which is the m80
direction). Firecracker's vsock muxer connects to that path; it does
not create one on guest bind.

Leaf 1 (VERIFY) must close this gap before any other leaf is started.
If verification shows the file is not created, the bead pivots:
- Plan A (file-stat probe) is dropped.
- m80-bgas (100ms / 60s constants) ships as the only `phase_12b`
  improvement, and m80-6gv9 (inotify) folds into a new file-watch
  target — likely the serial console + `GUESTD_READY` marker once
  `PUT /logger` is wired (a v0.2 epic).

## Design (conditional on verification passing)

Replace `phase_12b_ready_probe`'s polling loop with two phases:
1. Stat for `<vsock_uds>_<port>` at 10ms intervals (~1µs/probe vs the
   current full handshake cost). Existence => guest has bound.
2. Once the file appears, do the existing CONNECT/OK handshake one
   shot. The 5s read timeout still catches a guest that bound but
   never called accept().

The fallback-to-CONNECT/OK after stat returns is intentional: it
covers "bind succeeded but accept() not yet ready" without wedging
the probe. It is NOT premature complication.

## Brittleness contract

The companion-file naming is a Firecracker implementation detail, not
a stable API. The probe must:
- Document the exact Firecracker version range under which the naming
  was verified (in m80-vsock README under a new "Readiness contract"
  section).
- Keep CONNECT/OK as a hard fallback so a future Firecracker that
  changes the naming degrades to today's behavior, not failure.
- Re-verify on Firecracker upgrade as an explicit checklist item.

## Quick wins independent of this change

Tracked in m80-bgas (sibling): drop poll interval 500ms -> 100ms,
raise budget 30s -> 60s. m80-bgas should land first as a backstop.

## Acceptance (rolled-up)

- Leaf 1 verifies (or refutes) host-visible companion-file creation
  on a real KVM host under the in-tree Firecracker version.
- If verification passes: `phase_12b` uses the stat probe; CONNECT/OK
  becomes a one-shot post-stat handshake; latency from `InstanceStart`
  PUT to `Channel` returning `Ok` < 1s on idle host.
- m80-vsock README and m80-firecracker README updated to document the
  new readiness contract and its brittleness.
- Smoke test still passes; the simulated-load flake disappears or is
  documented as out-of-scope.

## Sibling beads

- m80-bgas (P2): the polling-constants-only quick win. Lands first.
- m80-6gv9 (P2): inotify upgrade. Stacks on top of m80-tv7i.
close_reason: premise-refuted: Firecracker creates `<uds>_<port>` only when GUEST initiates outbound (see firecracker muxer.rs:619-641). Host-side stat-poll on guest bind() is impossible. Empirical confirmed: 25s lifecycle observation showed only `vsock.sock` exists, no `vsock.sock_9001`. Verification: docs/verifications/m80-tv7i.1-vsock-companion-file.md. Pivot: m80-7tpy becomes primary readiness path (its mechanism is exactly what the source code supports — host pre-listens on `<uds>_<port>`, guest connects out).

title: VERIFY: probe whether Firecracker creates <vsock_uds>_<port> on guest bind()
description:
Gating leaf for m80-tv7i. Before any implementation work, verify on a
real KVM host that Firecracker creates a host-visible file at
`<vsock_uds>_<port>` when (and only when) m80-guestd executes
`VsockListener::bind((VMADDR_CID_ANY, 9001))`.

## Why this is the first leaf

Firecracker's documented vsock semantics describe `<uds>_<port>` as
the **host-side listener** for **guest-initiated** outbound
connections, not as an artifact of a guest bind. If verification
refutes the premise, the rest of m80-tv7i must be re-planned (likely
collapsing to m80-bgas + a future serial-console-watch leaf under
m80-6gv9 once `PUT /logger` is wired).

Do NOT skip this leaf. Do NOT start IMPL until this leaf is closed.

## Procedure

1. Boot the existing `end_to_end_real_kvm` test to a Running
   sandbox (or run `scripts/smoke.sh` once and pause it before
   `stop()` — easiest way to get a live VM).
2. Locate the host-side jail directory:
   `<run_root>/<vm_id>/firecracker/<vm_id>/root/`
3. Stat the candidate companion path:
   `<jail>/vsock.sock_9001`
4. Record three observations on a real KVM host running the
   in-tree Firecracker version:
   - Does the path exist after `InstanceStart` returns?
   - Does it exist after the guest has bound but before any host
     CONNECT/OK?
   - When in the boot sequence does it first appear (timestamp
     vs `InstanceStart` PUT)?
5. Cross-check against a guest variant that does NOT bind port 9001
   (temporarily comment out the bind in m80-guestd, rebuild rootfs,
   relaunch). If the file appears anyway, the file is unrelated to
   guest bind.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Manual run on KVM host produces a yes/no answer with timestamps,
      captured in a comment on this bead via `br update --notes`.
- [ ] If yes: the exact path format and creation timing are recorded
      (e.g., "appears within 5ms of guestd `bind()`; persists until
      VM stop"). This unblocks the IMPL leaf.
- [ ] If no: this bead is closed with `--reason "premise-refuted"`,
      the parent m80-tv7i is closed with the same reason, and a new
      bead is filed under m80-6gv9 to investigate the
      `PUT /logger`-based serial console watch as the next-best
      latency win.
- [ ] No code changes land from this leaf — observation only.

## Files / paths

- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch.rs` — `phase_12b_ready_probe`,
  `vsock_uds = jail.jail_path.join("vsock.sock")`
- `crates/m80-guestd/src/main.rs:57` — `VsockListener::bind_with_cid_port(VMADDR_CID_ANY, port)`
- `scripts/smoke.sh` — easy harness for getting a Running VM
- Firecracker upstream vsock doc:
  https://github.com/firecracker-microvm/firecracker/blob/main/docs/vsock.md

## Out of scope

- Writing a Rust integration test (see TEST-INT leaf).
- Touching `phase_12b_ready_probe`.
- Documenting the contract in READMEs (see DOCS leaf).

Empirical confirmed: 25s lifecycle observation showed only `vsock.sock` exists, no `vsock.sock_9001`. Verification: docs/verifications/m80-tv7i.1-vsock-companion-file.md. title: IMPL: stat-based two-phase ready probe in phase_12b
description:
Replace the polling loop in `phase_12b_ready_probe` with a two-phase
probe: stat the companion file, then do one CONNECT/OK handshake.

BLOCKED on m80-tv7i.1 (VERIFY) closing with a "yes" outcome.

## Today (crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch.rs:423)

- `READY_POLL_INTERVAL = 500ms`, `READY_TIMEOUT = 30s`
- Each loop iteration calls `Channel::open_uds_only` even when
  Firecracker has not yet seen guestd bind.

## After

- Phase A: stat `<vsock_uds_parent>/vsock.sock_<GUEST_PORT_DEFAULT>`
  at 10ms intervals until it exists, capped at the overall ready
  deadline.
- Phase B: a single `Channel::open_uds_only(vsock_uds, port)` call,
  reusing the existing 5s read timeout to catch a guest that bound
  but didn't `accept()`.
- New constants colocated with the existing ones:
  ```
  const STAT_POLL_INTERVAL: Duration = Duration::from_millis(10);
  ```
  Keep `READY_TIMEOUT` here — the budget is the parent's job; let
  m80-bgas own the 30s -> 60s change. No constants change here that
  m80-bgas also touches.
- The companion-port computation lives next to the probe (don't
  add a public `companion_path()` helper to m80-vsock yet — three
  near-identical lines beat a generic helper per CLAUDE.md).

## Fallback

If Phase A times out without the file appearing, fall back to a
single CONNECT/OK attempt before returning `VsockError::NotReady`.
Rationale: a future Firecracker that drops the companion file should
degrade to today's behavior, not fail outright. Document the
fallback as the brittleness escape hatch.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `phase_12b_ready_probe` rewritten in two phases as described.
- [ ] No new public surface on m80-vsock (the stat is host-side
      orchestration; m80-vsock continues to expose only
      `Channel::open` / `open_uds_only` / `watch_ready_marker`).
- [ ] Existing unit tests in m80-vsock unchanged.
- [ ] `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` clean.
- [ ] No `unsafe`. No new dependencies.
- [ ] Behavior doc at `docs/behaviors/lifecycle/ready-probe.md`
      describes the two-phase flow + fallback.

title: TEST-INT: real-KVM latency benchmark — InstanceStart -> Channel Ok < 1s
description:

elapsed time from `InstanceAction::InstanceStart` PUT returning to
`phase_12b_ready_probe` returning `Ok(Channel)`. Pins the latency
target so a future regression (or a Firecracker version that drops

The test must:
- Run the same `Backend::new` + `admit` + `launch` path as the
  existing test.
- Capture an `Instant` immediately before `client.instance_action`
  and another immediately after `phase_12b_ready_probe` returns —

title: Per-VM rootfs cloning
description:
[CLOSED 2026-05-04 — PREMISE REFUTED]

Original premise: each VM gets a private byte-for-byte copy of the base ext4 under its run-dir. Refuted by direct measurement (727 ms storage_prep per launch, ~256 MiB working-set churn) and by docs/exploration/firecracker-shared-rootfs.md showing N-VM read-only sharing of the same host file is safe and explicitly supported by Firecracker.

Superseded by m80-ovrl: shared RO base file (single inode, page-cache deduplicated) + per-VM sparse ext4 overlay + in-guest overlayfs. The four sub-leaves (cloning, parent-dir creation, base-identity pre-clone verify, CopyRootfs error) are obsolete.

title: Env var schema
description:
Contract: the accepted m80 env schema is exact and case-sensitive. title: Drop-in config.d/ directory support for m80 config (deep TOML merge)
description:
Deferred config layering support for /etc/m80/config.d/*.toml and the user-config equivalent. This is not a WRA0 image/profile-selection gate: the base env/config schema and loading order are already captured by m80-v7t.1, m80-v7t.2, and m80-v7t.3.

## Reference

Kata's config drop-in support deep-merges TOML files in lexicographic order. That pattern is useful once m80 has nested profile/image config, but the current m80 loader has only flat top-level backend keys.

## Scope

- Wait until m80-lt15.18 defines the image/profile config schema.
- Add system and user config.d layers in a documented position before env vars.
- If nested config exists by then, deep-table merge recursively; scalars overwrite; arrays replace. If config remains flat, keep the implementation flat and fail closed on unknown keys.
- Lexicographic file order; missing config.d directory is not an error; parse errors and unknown keys are errors.
- m80 config show reflects the merged result and source labels.

## Acceptance

- Tests pin lexicographic ordering and source precedence.
- Tests pin fail-closed behavior for parse errors and unknown keys.
- Documentation states exactly where config.d sits in the precedence chain.
- The bead does not block m80 run profile/image selection.

title: m80-bench: --diff <baseline.json> for per-phase regression detection during perf iteration
description:
Make perf iteration cheap. cc2aed2 added per-phase timing instrumentation; the obvious next step is comparing two runs.

## Why

During a perf push (e.g. m80-rrp.3 snapshot work, m80-bgas poll cadence), the workflow is "change something, run bench, eyeball numbers, did it help?" Eyeballing two columns of timings is error-prone and slow. Tooling beats vigilance.

## Scope

- m80-bench --json emits per-phase timings as a structured document (uses the m80-bpuf envelope).
- m80-bench --diff <baseline.json> runs the bench, then prints a per-phase delta table: phase | baseline_p50 | new_p50 | delta_us | delta_pct, sorted by abs(delta_us) desc.
- Color the deltas (red regression, green improvement) when stdout is a tty.
- Threshold flag: --fail-on-regress=10pct exits non-zero if any phase regresses past threshold (CI-friendly).

## Out of scope

- Persistent benchmark database (just files).
- Cross-machine baseline normalization (compare same host).

## Acceptance

- m80-bench --json > a.json; (apply change); m80-bench --diff a.json shows the delta.
- --fail-on-regress threshold tested.
- README of bench script + scripts/bench.sh documents the workflow.
notes: Implemented 2026-05-05 in commit cdc46d9. scripts/bench-summary.py (791 LOC, 31 unittest cases) with compute/summarize/diff subcommands. bench-cold-launch.sh writes per-run CSVs to mktemp dir for clean compute input, auto-saves snapshot to benches/snapshots/<ts>.json with latest.json symlink. Envelope shape {version:1, data:...} matches m80-bpuf intent. --fail-on-regress for CI gating. ANSI-colored tty output. Stdlib only.

title: Cold fresh launch performance exploration
description:
Explore true cold fresh launch performance after the warm-pool/persistent/snapshot paths have landed. This epic is not an alternative to warm pool; it is the residual cold-start improvement lane for cases that must boot a brand-new VM.

Current measured baseline on 2026-05-05:
- minimal cold launch post-storage pivot: about 1517 ms P50 idle
- storage prep after RO-base/overlay pivot: about 216 ms P50
- stripped kernel only bought about 100 ms, so more blind kernel trimming is low confidence
- direct snapshot restore is about 274 ms P50 idle and warm-pool allocation is about 21 ms typical, so cold-launch work must prove value with phase evidence

Angles:
1. guest-ready path reduction: reduce what PID 1 / guestd must do before readiness
2. pre-created overlay/rootfs artifacts: remove residual per-VM mkfs/template setup where safe
3. Firecracker setup/API path audit: quantify and trim jailer/materialization/REST/device setup
4. direct/no-jailer launch experiment: measure the ceiling, not necessarily productize it

Non-goals:
- Replacing warm pool, direct snapshot restore, or persistent VM routing
- Adapter-level policy or agent semantics
- Hidden compatibility fallbacks or tolerant launch behavior
- More kernel trimming without phase evidence

Acceptance:
- Each angle has a concrete measurement artifact, a yes/no recommendation, and either a narrow implementation bead or an explicit dead-end note
- Cold-launch docs summarize the residual bottleneck stack after the four explorations
- No implementation bead is accepted without idle and loaded evidence, or a clear reason the loaded cell is not meaningful

title: BASELINE: phase-profile cold fresh launch residual bottlenecks
description:
Build the common measurement baseline that every cold-launch exploration leaf must use. The point is to stop debating hypotheses and make phase deltas comparable.

Scope:
- Extend or reuse the existing cold-launch benchmark to emit per-phase timing for minimal/stock and minimal/stripped where available.
- Record at least phase_3_storage_prep, phase_4_jailer_materialize, phase_9_jailer_exec, REST PUT/device setup, InstanceStart, ready signal/guestd accept, and total wallclock.
- Run idle and loaded cells with the same stress-ng shape used by existing perf docs.
- Keep output machine-readable JSON plus a compact markdown summary.

Acceptance:
- docs/perf/cold-launch.md or a dedicated docs/behaviors/lifecycle/cold-launch-phase-profile.md has the baseline table.
- Raw JSON includes N, host load, kernel kind, image kind, per-phase P50/P95/max, and success count.
- The four child exploration leaves cite this baseline instead of inventing their own numbers.

title: EXPLORE: guest-ready path reduction before cold-launch readiness
description:
Explore whether the guest-ready path can be shortened without changing m80 semantics. This is the most plausible cold-launch win because current evidence puts the ready/boot side near the largest remaining chunk.

Scope:
- Profile guestd PID-1 startup before it emits readiness: pseudo-fs mounts, overlay pivot, workspace mount, signal/reaper setup, exec listener bind, ready signal.
- Add temporary structured timestamps if existing logs cannot separate these steps; keep the diagnostic surface if it proves useful.
- Evaluate variants such as ready-before-nonessential-setup, static/initramfs guestd path, delayed workspace mount for no-workspace launches, and smaller busybox/mount sequence.
- Preserve correctness: readiness must mean the exec listener can accept and run the documented command shape; no false-ready state.

Non-goals:
- Removing diagnostics visibility to save a few milliseconds
- Adapter-level lazy workspace semantics
- Further kernel config trimming unless the profile proves guest userspace is not dominant

Acceptance:
- Idle and loaded phase deltas identify the largest pre-ready guest steps.
- A recommended implementation slice is created only if it can plausibly save at least 100 ms P50 or materially reduce loaded-tail failures.
- If the best option is ready-before-finish, the bead states the exact invariant that still makes readiness honest.
acceptance_criteria:
- The baseline artifact identifies whether the aggregate guest-ready phase is a dominant cold-launch bottleneck on idle and loaded cells.
- If existing host-side phase data cannot split guest PID-1 substeps, create a narrow diagnostics implementation bead before any optimization bead.
- A recommended optimization slice is created only after substep evidence shows a plausible >=100 ms P50 save or materially reduced loaded-tail failures.
- If a future option is ready-before-finish, the bead states the exact invariant that still makes readiness honest.

title: EXPLORE: pre-created overlay/rootfs artifacts for cold launch
description:
Explore the host-artifact angle for true cold fresh launch: pre-created overlay/rootfs artifacts, including whether the existing m80-f2zc.10 overlay-template bead is sufficient or whether a broader artifact pool is justified.

Current evidence:
- Storage pivot removed the full rootfs copy, but phase_3_storage_prep is still about 216 ms P50.
- Existing leaf m80-f2zc.10 already targets an empty overlay ext4 template with reflink/copy fallback.

Scope:
- Measure how much of phase_3_storage_prep is overlay sparse create, mkfs.ext4, scratch preparation, and host metadata work.
- Evaluate three options: implement m80-f2zc.10 as-is; add a bounded pool of pre-created overlay images; do nothing because warm pool already absorbs this path.
- Include filesystem reality: reflink availability, plain-copy cost, template metadata identity, run-root capacity, cleanup on crash.
- Keep hard-cutover and fail-closed behavior: stale/wrong-size templates are errors, not silently reused.

Acceptance:
- Recommendation says whether m80-f2zc.10 is enough, should be expanded, or should remain lower priority.
- If expanded, create/update a narrow implementation bead with exact template/pool contract and tests.
- Benchmark target is explicit: expected phase_3_storage_prep P50/P95 delta and total cold-launch impact.

title: EXPLORE: Firecracker setup and REST path cold-launch audit
description:
Audit the host-side Firecracker setup path for cold fresh launch. This is expected to be a smaller-win lane unless phase timing proves otherwise, but it can uncover simple sequencing or syscall waste.

Scope:
- Break down jailer materialization, cgroup setup, jailer exec, Firecracker API socket readiness, REST PUT sequence, drive/vsock/network device setup, and InstanceStart.
- Compare minimal NoEgress with workspace/no-workspace and stock/stripped where relevant.
- Look for conservative changes: fewer REST calls where Firecracker supports combining, avoid redundant filesystem/stat work, delay nonessential diagnostics setup only if visibility is preserved, remove dead waits.
- Document any API limitation where Firecracker itself is the fixed cost.

Non-goals:
- Bypassing jailer in production; that belongs to the no-jailer measurement leaf.
- Changing m80 security/resource invariants for small wins.

Acceptance:
- Per-phase table identifies any host setup phase above 50 ms P50 or with a loaded-tail problem.
- Each proposed change has an expected delta and a regression test/bench plan.
- If no meaningful host setup win exists, close with evidence and no implementation follow-up.

title: WRA0 Protobuf wire hard cutover
description:
Hard-cut the host<->guest wire from NDJSON JSON/base64 envelopes to a length-prefixed protobuf envelope with explicit byte-stream messages. The goal is to stop exposing downstream users to the bad shape where bulk bytes are one JSON response object, while preserving m80's generic VM-mechanics boundary.

The new contract is: small control messages and bulk byte movement share one typed protobuf envelope; bulk stdout/stderr/PTY/file/log data moves as bounded chunks with terminal success/error frames. No compatibility shim, no dual decoder, no fallback to the v0.1 NDJSON protocol.

Early work is test-first. The first lane creates red two-way tests for host->guest and guest->host byte movement that reproduce the current 4 MiB/base64 failure and define the desired protobuf behavior before the implementation lands.

## Success Criteria

- m80-proto exposes protobuf schema/types and length-prefixed frame helpers; NDJSON/base64 framing is removed from the active wire.
- Host and guest agree on one protocol version and fail closed on mismatch.
- File read/write, exec stdout/stderr, PTY, diagnostics/log stream, metrics, shutdown, and cancellation/control frames use the new envelope shape or are explicitly documented as out of scope.
- E2E tests prove 5 MiB+ guest->host and host->guest transfers complete without OversizedPayload, EOF masking, byte corruption, or lost terminal status.
- Crate READMEs and behavior docs describe the new wire as streaming-first and protobuf-backed.

title: WRA0.1 Test-first two-way byte transfer contract

## Success Criteria

- Tests intentionally fail on the current NDJSON/base64 single-response implementation for the large-read case.
- Tests cover both directions, terminal success/error frames, and diagnostic visibility when a transfer fails.
- Real-KVM E2E coverage is present for the 5 MiB repro; faster protocol/unit tests cover frame boundaries and malformed peers.

title: Process-wrapper product surface: constrained host view
description:
Grand epic for the user-facing m80 product surface: run a host-like process with an explicitly constrained view of filesystem, environment, runtime image, network, and lifetime. The VM remains an implementation detail.

End state:
- `m80 run [visibility/effect/world/profile options] -- <cmd>` is the front door. Pipe mode streams stdout/stderr in real time and preserves exit code. PTY mode supports TUIs.
- Egress, workspace, cwd, env, stdin, scratch, writeback, credentials, selected image/profile, and warm/cold lifetime are named as process visibility/effect/world policies, not VM machinery.
- Warm execution is exposed as an optional lifecycle acceleration with an explicit resident owner; no hidden daemon and no silent cold fallback.
- First-run UX can get from install/artifacts to `m80 run -- echo hello` without archaeology.
- Debuggability is built in: request_id, typed errors, JSON error envelopes, run-root inspection, console/diagnostics correlation, and KVM e2e smoke.

Non-goals:
- Agent tool semantics in m80 core.
- Docker-compatible lifecycle UX as the primary model.
- Hidden daemon/process manager.
- Silent fallback from requested policy to a weaker/different policy.
- Implicit runtime package installation or OCI image pulling in `m80 run`.

Acceptance:
- Child epics cover command contract, visibility/effects, image/profile selection, pipe streaming, egress, PTY/TUI, warm lifetime, config/errors/diagnostics, quickstart, docs/examples, and e2e smoke.
- Top-level README/help teach the constrained-process model.
- The graph has a single ready first gate for command contract and no dependency cycles.
notes: closure audit 2026-05-06: all parent-child dependents are closed (lt15 CLI facade/warm/PTY/streaming/profile, 9fcy request_id diagnostics, 4ef errors, v7t config/discovery, exy/xbn networking policy surfaces, 5vha streaming, bpuf JSON envelope, 6jni release artifacts/DX, rwl5 quickstart, wra0.1 docs/examples/help). Real verification: private GitHub repo moradology/m80, tag v0.2.6 release artifacts workflow passed, main CI run 25416097272 passed fmt/build/test/clippy, release asset checksum verified after download, sudo quickstart against downloaded artifact printed hello. Related open qokt and 6zim remain explicitly non-core adapter/file-ops follow-ups, not WRA0 acceptance blockers.

title: Product docs: constrained-process landing page, examples, and help
description:
Turn the WRA0 product decision into the user-facing spine for m80. SmolVM is stronger at first contact because the README, examples, and help text all lead with runnable workloads; m80 must keep its stronger crate-contract discipline while adding the missing landing path.

Scope:
- Rewrite the top-level README top fold around `m80 run [policy] -- <cmd>` as the primary product story. The dossier intro moves lower or links out; it does not remain the first viewport.
- Add small runnable examples that map to WRA0 policies: echo/no workspace, workspace visibility, egress none/outbound, and interactive TTY once that lane lands. Examples should be command-first and avoid a new Smolfile-style workload DSL.
- Keep crate READMEs as contracts; this bead owns cross-cutting user orientation and top-level help wording.
- Help text stays concise and process-oriented. Do not embed the entire agent/project manual in clap output unless a later bead proves the UX case.

Acceptance:
- README opens with generic Firecracker sandboxing as a constrained process wrapper and includes a copy-paste `m80 run -- echo hello` quickstart.
- `docs/behaviors/cli/product-surface.md` or equivalent explains pipe mode, PTY mode, egress, workspace, writeback, warm, and diagnostics as user-facing policies.
- `examples/` contains at least echo, workspace, and egress examples with exact commands.
- `m80 --help` and `m80 run --help` lead with constrained-process language, not VM lifecycle management.
- The docs call out runtime availability honestly: the requested command must exist in the selected image/profile; m80 does not pull OCI images or install packages implicitly.

title: Cold fresh launch performance exploration
description:
Explore true cold fresh launch performance after the warm-pool/persistent/snapshot paths have landed. This epic is not an alternative to warm pool; it is the residual cold-start improvement lane for cases that must boot a brand-new VM.

Current measured baseline on 2026-05-05:
- minimal cold launch post-storage pivot: about 1517 ms P50 idle
- storage prep after RO-base/overlay pivot: about 216 ms P50
- stripped kernel only bought about 100 ms, so more blind kernel trimming is low confidence
- direct snapshot restore is about 274 ms P50 idle and warm-pool allocation is about 21 ms typical, so cold-launch work must prove value with phase evidence

Angles:
1. guest-ready path reduction: reduce what PID 1 / guestd must do before readiness
2. pre-created overlay/rootfs artifacts: remove residual per-VM mkfs/template setup where safe
3. Firecracker setup/API path audit: quantify and trim jailer/materialization/REST/device setup
4. direct/no-jailer launch experiment: measure the ceiling, not necessarily productize it

Non-goals:
- Replacing warm pool, direct snapshot restore, or persistent VM routing
- Adapter-level policy or agent semantics
- Hidden compatibility fallbacks or tolerant launch behavior
- More kernel trimming without phase evidence

Acceptance:
- Each angle has a concrete measurement artifact, a yes/no recommendation, and either a narrow implementation bead or an explicit dead-end note
- Cold-launch docs summarize the residual bottleneck stack after the four explorations
- No implementation bead is accepted without idle and loaded evidence, or a clear reason the loaded cell is not meaningful
notes: duplicate draft superseded by completed epic m80-w4vc; no children or dependencies
